items.text: Schwab states the Advisor Services segment provides custodial, trading, banking and trust, and support services to independent registered investment advisors (RIAs), independent retirement advisors, and recordkeepers.
items.quote: The Advisor Services segment provides custodial, trading, banking and trust, and support services to independent registered investment advisors (RIAs), independent retirement advisors, and recordkeepers.

items.text: Schwab states RIAs and their clients have access to its broad range of wealth services and that, as custodian, Schwab earns revenue from underlying client assets and does not charge the RIA or end client a custody fee.
items.quote: By functioning as the custodian, Schwab earns revenue associated with the underlying client assets, predominantly through net interest revenue and asset management and administration fees. In this capacity, we do not charge the RIA or end client a custody fee.

items.text: Schwab states it serves more than 16,000 firms representing $5.8 trillion in assets with a platform that brings together custody, trading, banking and lending capabilities, technology, and dedicated service and support.
items.quote: Today, we serve more than 16,000 firms representing $5.8 trillion in assets with a platform that brings together custody, trading, banking and lending capabilities, technology and dedicated service and support.

items.text: Schwab states Advisor Services is in a position of strength and remains a driving force for Schwab, with $5.2T in client assets, 16K advisory firms, and 3.9M households, and #1 in RIA custodial assets.
items.quote: Advisor Services is in a position of strength & remains a driving force for Schwab. $5.2T Client Assets 16K Advisory Firms Households 3.9M in RIA Custodial Assets #1

items.text: Schwab states Schwab Advisor Services provides custody, trading, and the support services of Charles Schwab & Co., Inc. to independent investment advisors.
items.quote: Schwab Advisor Services provides custody, trading, and the support services of Charles Schwab & Co., Inc. ("Schwab"), member SIPC, to independent investment advisors and Charles Schwab Investment Management, Inc. ("CSIM").

cells.reason: Passages describe the RIA custody/advisor services business and its offering in Schwab's own terms.

cells.label: fact

items.text: Schwab states its strategic priority is to be the leading RIA support ecosystem, providing wealth tools, investment/lending products, and technology in addition to custody and service.
items.quote: The leading RIA support ecosystem to help advisors serve their clients, providing wealth tools, investment / lending products, & technology in addition to custody & service

items.text: Schwab states it is deepening relationships with the 16,000 RIA firms it serves by building a broader support ecosystem that extends beyond custody alone, including growing lending support, alternatives capability, and an expanded institutional no-transaction-fee mutual fund platform.
items.quote: we're deepening relationships with the 16,000 RIA firms we serve by building a broader support ecosystem that extends beyond custody alone to add value for RIAs. We've grown our lending support, alternatives capability, and expanded our institutional no-transaction fee mutual fund platform

items.text: Schwab states it is enhancing its digital experiences across RIA workflows such as move money, account open, and account maintenance, while modernizing tools on its advisor platform.
items.quote: In Advisor Services, we're continuing to enhance our digital experiences across RIA workflows like move money, account open and account maintenance while also modernizing tools on our adviser platform.

items.text: Schwab states that in advisor services it is adding support and capabilities for RIAs of all sizes while also helping new advisors transition to independence.
items.quote: In advisor services, we are adding support and capabilities for RIAs of all sizes while also helping new advisors transition to independence.

items.text: Schwab states it is investing in banking and lending for RIAs as the natural provider of those capabilities and is just getting started with its banking journey for RIAs.
items.quote: And the RIAs want to be able to match that, and we're the natural provider of that... I think we're just getting started with our banking journey, and I couldn't be more excited about it.

items.text: Schwab states it launched Advisor ProDirect, a fee-based, membership-driven offer designed to support independence for new RIAs.
items.quote: In our advisor services business, we launched Advisor ProDirect, a fee-based, membership-driven offer designed to support independence for new RIAs.

cells.reason: Passages state Schwab's strategic priorities for the RIA/advisor services business.

cells.label: fact

items.text: Schwab states that in the Advisor Services arena it competes with institutional custodians, wirehouses, regional and independent broker-dealers, fintech custodians, banks, and trust companies.
items.quote: In the Advisor Services arena, we compete with institutional custodians, wirehouses, regional and independent broker-dealers, fintech custodians, banks, and trust companies.

items.text: Schwab's CEO states that RIAs compete against the wealth divisions of wirehouses and that wirehouses are doing a better job of leveraging their banking capabilities.
items.quote: They do, from time to time, compete against the wealth divisions of wirehouses... the wirehouses are doing a better job of leveraging their banking capabilities.

items.text: Schwab's CEO states that independent advisors are competing against wirehouses that typically have strong banks attached to their advice.
items.quote: If you put yourself in the shoes of the independent advisor, they're competing against wirehouses that typically have really strong banks attached to their advice.

cells.reason: Schwab's 10-K and CEO statements name the competitor categories and wirehouses it competes with in the RIA custody/advisor services arena.

items.text: Schwab's CEO states that Schwab has changed the minimums for long/short strategies and throttled growth to some extent.
items.quote: as we look to October, where we have changed the minimums for long/short and throttled growth to some extent, the growth has in no way slowed at all in terms of AS NNA.

items.text: Schwab states it limited long-short offerings to clients with at least $10 million in assets, curtailing their use by many advisors.
items.quote: That led the firm to limit long-short offerings only to clients with at least $10 million in assets, curtailing their use by many advisors.

items.text: Schwab states it is reducing the Schwab Advisor Network referral network by raising the bar for participation to only clients with over $5 million and RIAs with at least $500 million in AUM.
items.quote: reducing the Schwab Advisor Network referral network by raising the bar for participation to only clients with over $5 million and RIAs with at least $500 million in AUM.

items.text: A Schwab spokesperson confirms the asset minimum for client referrals in Schwab Advisor Network has changed from $2 million to $5 million, effective Jan. 5, 2027.
items.quote: the asset minimum for client referrals in Schwab Advisor Network (SAN) has changed from $2 million to $5 million, effective Jan. 5, 2027.

items.text: A Schwab spokesperson states that, following a review of Forge Global after its acquisition, Schwab has reached an agreement to divest the Forge Trust business, a self-directed IRA custodian.
items.quote: Following that review, we've reached an agreement to divest the Forge Trust business. We are committed to Forge's private markets platform and are excited about the capabilities it brings to Schwab clients.

cells.reason: Schwab statements describe pullbacks in RIA-related areas (long/short limits, SAN referral reductions, Forge Trust divestiture); no Schwab statement in the passages says it is losing ground.
